{"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"LEVIED BY flo2 — a mutating call carries who made it, and the server records that it happened, without the caller having to remember","priority":"high","provenance":"authored","statement":"A REQUIREMENT LEVIED ON REFLOW2 BY A CONSUMER, not reflow2's own intent — recorded at `proposed`, which is the only status a consumer's ask may land at. Relayed 2026-09-22 through the dev_reflow2 hub session, which is itself the first live exercise of `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency`.

ITS HOME ON THEIR SIDE: flo2, graph `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`, on `ifc:caller-attribution-and-automatic-change-journal`, which flo2 has designated `required`. Also their feedback log F31.

WHAT THEY ASK, in two clauses:
1. **Accept a caller identity and remember it for the session** — a `contributor_id` supplied at initialize or set once per session, taken purely on trust.
2. **Automatically journal every mutating call** — what changed and who — without the caller writing a ChangeEvent.

flo2 stresses: this is ATTRIBUTION, NOT AUTHENTICATION. They prove identity at their own gateway and explicitly do not want reflow2 to grow auth.

WHY THEY NEED IT, in their words: flo2 settled that a design's history IS reflow2's ChangeEvents. Under "one design, two doors" — a chat app and coding agents on the same design — writes through the developer door arrive unattributed and unrecorded, so "what changed while I was away" is confidently incomplete. The cost is already measured and already recorded in THIS graph: `fact:flo2-shipped-two-days-of-work-with-no-change-event-and-rebuilt-the-history-from-git-a-day-late` — two days of work with no ChangeEvent behind it, found at a reconcile pass, rebuilt from git a day late.

THEIR DONE, stated as a test rather than a feeling: two different people write through one design; reading the graph ALONE, every change is attributed correctly; and the number of recorded changes equals the number of mutating calls.

⭐ AND THEIR OWN COUNTER-ARGUMENT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MOVES THIS: an automatic journal is complete but NOISY. So they ask for two tiers — an automatic floor that cannot be forgotten, plus authored ChangeEvents on top — and say that **if only one ships, the floor matters more.**

⇒ THAT ANSWERS THE STANDING OBJECTION ON `dec:idea-should-the-server-journal-every-write-itself`, whose whole position is "the what and the who are cheap; the WHY is what this design insists on and no automatic journal can supply it." The two-tier split concedes that objection entirely and routes around it: the floor never claims to carry a why, and the authored layer that does carry one is untouched. It is a materially better proposal than the one triaged earlier the same day.

🛑 WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT IS NOT: it is not reflow2 agreeing. It lands `proposed` because `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is ENFORCED — a consumer may ask for anything and settle nothing, and an agent relaying the ask may settle even less. Anthony's word moves it. The two open Decisions above are where the argument lives; this node is the ASK, so that a later reader can tell "flo2 needs this" from "reflow2 decided this".","status":"proposed"}
